role.both: default Claude owner and advisor; only Micro implementation and deterministic checks go lower. role.both: fast Claude rung below Opus medium. High (42; FrontierCode 2.0 26, Terminal-Bench 4.0 44; 9 s to first token) for bounded semantic workers and allowance fallbacks; above that, Opus medium beats it on the index, FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (48; 33/53) with fewer output tokens (44k vs 58k). Skip low; reserve medium for tiny semantic implementation with an explicit result and a direct check. For general work, Haiku 5.5 medium/high come within a point of their index (25/30 vs 26/31) at a fraction of the cost. From xhigh up, Opus beats it for less: Opus high 52 with 60k output tokens vs Sonnet xhigh 50 with 122k. Sonnet xhigh matches Opus high on FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (36/57), so it is an implementation fallback after an Opus-family usage limit, not an allowance saver. No research synthesis. Claude Code defaults it to medium, so set the effort explicitly. If Sonnet 5.5 is unavailable in the client or account, take the matching Opus 5.5 route (medium for medium or high).

role.both: cheapest Claude worker and the Micro owner for mechanical edits. Above Luna at every effort (19–36 vs 10–28). Low (19) for exact extraction; high (30; FrontierCode 2.0 23, Terminal-Bench 4.0 22) for specified edits and deterministic checks. Xhigh (35) is usable when the task fits and ~56 s to first answer is acceptable (136k output tokens per index task); avoid max (226k, ~185 s). Token-heavy at every effort (28k at low): keep packets compact; Anthropic's API rate rises 5× above 100k prompt tokens, with no published plan-allowance multiplier. No knowledge-heavy, ambiguous or consequential final calls. If Haiku 5.5 is unavailable in the client or account, take Sonnet 5.5 high for the same work.

role.both: GPT-6.2 Sol, the default OpenAI owner and advisor for routine work. Medium (53; FrontierCode 2.0 41, Terminal-Bench 4.0 56; about 3 s to first token) for Micro plans, Plan Next, Bounded work and settled Standard implementation with checks that cover the changed behavior. High (55; 40/59) for Standard plans and reviews, diagnosis, design judgment and terminal investigation. Xhigh (56; 43/56) is the escalation for repository work when high falls short: the API suite gives high the better Terminal-Bench 4.0 (59 vs 56), while Codex in Coding Agent Index v2.1 gives xhigh the better Terminal-Bench 4.1 (58 vs 54). For Complex implementation, choose by the task and use strong acceptance checks. Max (57; 44/60) is a task-specific escalation when its measured advantage matters: Codex favors xhigh over max (50 vs 49, 12.6 vs 17.5 min) and its SWE-Atlas-QnA score falls from 51 at xhigh to 46 at max, so prefer xhigh before max. Low (41; 31/38) only for short checked work, including mechanical edits with a direct checker. Knowledge-heavy synthesis goes to Opus 5.5 xhigh, or Astra high under its gate. Ultra is max plus automatic delegation, an orchestration mode, never for a child. If the client rejects GPT-6.2 Sol, update the client; if it is still unavailable, take the next capable route in the table.

role.both: GPT-6.2 Astra, the strongest OpenAI model, for Complex and Deep work only under its gate. Medium (57; FrontierCode 2.0 47, Terminal-Bench 4.0 59) equals Sol max and Opus xhigh on the index and fits Complex implementation with explicit invariants and strong checks; high (60; 47/60) leads Opus max (59) and covers Complex integration that needs judgment, Deep work and the hardest advice. High is its routing ceiling for owners, workers, advisors and escalations; xhigh and max stay in the tables as evidence only. If high falls short, narrow the problem or reroute to a capable Claude route. Every Astra use needs a demonstrated hard need, capable regular routes that failed or are unsuitable, and explicit per-scope user approval. Skip low (Sol medium beats it). One bounded call at a time; never parallel, never a fan-out worker, never ultra.

evidence.note: [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v5) (launched 2026-10-27; [leaderboard](https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models)): index / API cost per index task / seconds to first answer token (— = not published). v5 rescored every model, so never mix these values with Index v4.3.2 figures. All values are v5.0.1 (re-fetched 2026-11-08 unless a later reading is noted; most first-token times, a rolling 5-day average, re-read 2026-11-10 with scores, costs and tokens unchanged): v5.0.1 regraded one eval, moving a few index cells by a point, and first-token times follow Artificial Analysis Performance Benchmarking v3.0.0 (2026-11-03), so they differ from earlier snapshots. Cost is a rough within-provider allowance proxy, never a cross-provider currency; first-token time is API latency, not agent wall time.
